frequency_question: What proportion of major bilateral water-sharing treaty renewals or successor agreements are formally signed prior to or immediately upon the expiration of the predecessor treaty?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral treaties governing shared international rivers requiring renewal or renegotiation after a fixed multi-decade duration. Excludes unilateral declarations, non-binding memorandums without allocation quotas, and basins without prior formal treaties.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation and modifications (India-Pakistan)
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase protocols (Lesotho-South Africa)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; represents the most direct comparable asymmetric federal-state riparian treaty renewals globally.
known_gaps: Limited strictly to South Asian and comparable major developing-world asymmetric river basins to maintain relevance.
skeleton: Specific major bilateral water treaty renegotiations involving complex downstream-upstream asymmetry and domestic political transitions over a multi-decade span.
multiplier: 3 observed major asymmetric bilateral renegotiation episodes yielding successful successor frameworks or continuous operational protocols.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydro-diplomacy structural dynamics evolve slowly over decades, keeping this reference class stable through the end of the decade.
